scope_note: Deep public-evidence audit for Google Clarksville in Montgomery County, Tennessee. The review covered Tennessee Comptroller industrial-development-board PILOT filings for 2019-2025; Montgomery County parcel-linked stormwater files; Clarksville-Montgomery County Regional Planning Commission materials; state economic-development records; operator location, environmental, economic-impact and watershed materials; public workforce, contractor, procurement and recipient sources; and local fiscal, utility and public-service records. Twenty incremental quantitative observations are preserved: thirteen annual Foxman LLC estimated-actual-property-value stocks, a realized opening-period employee snapshot, a construction-workforce projection, and five recipient-specific community contributions. The PILOT values are neither assessed/taxable values nor taxes or PILOT payments, and the filings' blank payment fields are not interpreted as zero. The selected inventory key is one building, while property and environmental evidence is campus or company/county scoped and remains unallocated. Statewide investment and modeled impact totals, shared Alabama-Tennessee renewable capacity, regional watershed contributions, and proposals for later Building 13 work are excluded from canonical project records. A single optional synthesis reproduces the operator's 2024 Montgomery County water-consumption identity at unallocated location scope; no multiplier, supplier-retention, fiscal, public-cost, energy, payroll or causal county model is created.

project_updates.title: Project identity, boundary and operating chronology audit
project_updates.notes: Google's 2015 ownership statement, Montgomery County stormwater permits 13099, 13652, 14780 and 17507, the current operator milestone page, and 2026 county/RPC Foxman records were cross-checked. The evidence links Google/Foxman to map 009 parcel 014.01, documents phased site work in 2017-2019 and official opening in 2019, and distinguishes later Building 13 proposals from the selected inventory building.
project_updates.project_description: Google Clarksville is Google LLC's operating data-center campus at 1000 Boolean Drive (formerly 1000 Solar Way) in Clarksville, Montgomery County, Tennessee, on the former Hemlock Semiconductor site. Google announced its acquisition of the roughly 1,300-acre site in December 2015; county stormwater records show Foxman LLC phases SPC 1A-1C receiving grading approvals in 2017-2018, and Google reports that the data center officially opened in 2019. The project key maps one inventory building, but public PILOT filings and permit records describe the broader parcel 009-014.01 campus, including a separate 2026 Building 13 site review, so campus values are not allocated to the selected building.

project_updates.title: PILOT and property-value record audit, 2019-2025
project_updates.notes: Tennessee Comptroller annual IDB filings were searched for Foxman LLC, parcel 009 01401 000 and personal-property variants for 2019-2025. Thirteen estimated-actual-value stocks are retained; the 2022 report contains only the real-property row. Payment fields are blank across the reviewed rows, so no tax receipt, PILOT payment, abatement realization or net fiscal claim is created.

project_updates.title: Permit, planning and expansion audit
project_updates.notes: County stormwater current-project files and RPC agenda SR-14-2026 were searched using Foxman, Google, 1000 Solar Way, 1000 Boolean Drive and parcel 009-014.01. These sources establish project phases and a later 15,200-square-foot Building 13 proposal but publish no permit valuation, completed construction cost, procurement ledger, employment realization or operating utility increment.

project_updates.title: Investment and operator-impact audit
project_updates.notes: Google's current Tennessee page and Deloitte-prepared 2024 impact report were checked for Clarksville-specific realized capital, operations and fiscal amounts. More than $6 billion is explicitly statewide, while the report's more-than-$2.1-billion infrastructure input and $263-million GDP, 2,235-job and $169-million labor-income results are Tennessee-level contribution estimates; none is transcribed or re-modeled as a project or county observation.

project_updates.title: Operating workforce and payroll audit
project_updates.notes: Operator milestones, regional economic-development reporting, current careers materials and local employer references were searched for establishment headcount, FTEs, occupations, wages, payroll, residence and contractors. Only the January 2020 approximate 70-employee operating snapshot is retained. No annual series, payroll, wage, local-resident share or current establishment census was found.

project_updates.title: Construction labor and supplier/procurement audit
project_updates.notes: Groundbreaking coverage and federal EEOC records identify a projection of at least 1,000 construction workers and Whiting-Turner's general-contractor role from at least May 2018 through fall 2019. Searches did not locate project invoices, paid contract values, job-years, payroll, worker residence, subcontractor payments, vendor addresses or a local-purchase share, so no supplier or multiplier record is added.

project_updates.title: Water, wastewater and environmental audit
project_updates.notes: Google's 2025 Environmental Report location schedule and methodology were checked against Montgomery County and Clarksville utility/public works sources. The report gives 2024 Montgomery County withdrawal, discharge and consumption, but no selected-building split; discharge may be engineering-estimated. Municipal bill, meter, wastewater-fee, reclaimed-water, peak-day and infrastructure-cost records were not found. One optional synthesis preserves only the reported consumption identity and rounding at unallocated location scope.

project_updates.title: Electricity, renewable-energy and capacity audit
project_updates.notes: Operator location and impact materials, TVA references and local utility records were searched for facility kWh, peak MW, rate class, demand charges, power bills, substations, generators and operating emissions. The only quantitative renewable figure found was 308 MW shared across Alabama and Tennessee, with no Clarksville allocation; no canonical or modeled project energy amount is created.

project_updates.title: Community and recipient-record audit
project_updates.notes: Google, Deloitte, Austin Peay State University, Montgomery County and watershed-project sources were reconciled by recipient and period. Five bounded recipient amounts are retained. The broader $943,000 surrounding-community total, more-than-$1.5-million watershed total, statewide philanthropy, and multi-county program grants are excluded because geography or overlap cannot be reconciled without double counting.

project_updates.title: Fiscal receipts, incentives and public-cost audit
project_updates.notes: The state PILOT archive, county and city budgets/financial reports, assessment resources and economic-development materials were searched for project-linked tax bills, receipts, PILOT payments, abatements, compliance, infrastructure spending and marginal services. The leasehold mechanism is documented, but no numeric payment realization or same-scope public cost was found. Property-value stocks are not netted against unknown payments or costs, and no break-even or net-benefit model is created.

project_updates.title: County-outcome and causal-evidence audit
project_updates.notes: Federal BEA, BLS and Census county/industry series and the Deloitte statewide impact study were considered after direct project searches. Public county series do not isolate Google from Fort Campbell, population growth, other investment, the 2020 shock or later campus phases, and the available treatment timing does not support a governed causal design. No descriptive comparison gap, multiplier transfer or claimed county effect is added.
